passage:
I'm Gurpreet. On Monday morning our class group filled up with an edited photo of Madhuri's face stuck on a cartoon buffalo, and people were forwarding it with laughing faces. Madhuri walked in, saw phones being tucked away, and stopped at the door. Her face went pale and she sat down without a word.
At lunch she didn't eat. When I asked, she only said, "Whatever."
I sat next to her and asked if she wanted to take screenshots. She did. We blocked the account that started it, and she showed the pages to our class teacher. Madhuri never replied with a meme of her own. Later she told me she had felt hurt and exposed, and that saying it out loud helped. The teacher closed the group.

qa.q: What was Madhuri's face edited onto in the photo?
qa.a: It was edited onto a cartoon buffalo.

qa.q: What was Madhuri probably feeling when she walked in and saw phones being tucked away?
qa.a: She likely felt hurt and exposed, since her face went pale and she stopped at the door, and later she said so herself. 🤍

qa.q: What did Madhuri and Gurpreet do that avoided retaliation?
qa.a: They took screenshots, blocked the account that started it and showed the class teacher, instead of replying with another meme.

qa.q: How might the class teacher see the situation?
qa.a: The teacher probably sees a hurt student and a class group being misused, and takes it seriously because Madhuri came with the screenshots.

grounding: Shows a teen mocked with edited images who saves screenshots, blocks, tells a trusted adult and does not retaliate.

passage:
In Class 9, someone in our class chat posted a photo of me from sports day, edited so I had a pig's snout. Then another with my face on a buffalo. I'm Ganga, and I'll never forget the laughing emojis under them. Vikas had made the first one. Others added more.

I felt sick. Hot and exposed, like everyone was staring even when I was alone in my room. My first thought was to make one of Vikas, worse.

I didn't. My cousin had told me what to do once, and I did it: screenshots of everything, with names and times. Then I blocked Vikas and reported the posts on the app. The next morning I went straight to Mrs Joseph, our class teacher, and showed her.

She didn't say "ignore it." She said, "This is not your fault, Ganga. This is bullying." She took the screenshots to the principal that day, and Vikas's parents were called in.

It still stings sometimes. But I didn't become like them.

qa.q: What was edited onto Ganga's face in the first photo?
qa.a: A pig's snout was edited onto the photo.

qa.q: What was Ganga feeling when the edited photos were posted?
qa.a: Ganga felt sick, hurt and exposed, as if everyone was staring.

qa.q: What steps did Ganga take instead of retaliating?
qa.a: Ganga saved screenshots with names and times, blocked Vikas, reported the posts and told Mrs Joseph the next morning.

qa.q: How did Mrs Joseph respond, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Mrs Joseph said it was not Ganga's fault, named it as bullying and took it to the principal that day, so Ganga was believed and protected.

grounding: It shows a teen mocked with edited photos by classmates, feeling hurt and exposed, who does not retaliate, saves screenshots, blocks, reports and tells a trusted adult.

passage:
Class teacher's note, 10A, Monday

Lalremsiami came to me before assembly with her phone and a printed sheet. Over the weekend, a group of boys had posted memes in the class chat mocking the way she speaks, with captions in a fake accent, and one edited photo of her face on a cartoon. Pradeep had started it; others joined in.

She spoke very quietly, but her hands were steady. "I didn't reply. I took screenshots, blocked them and reported the posts. My mother said to bring it to you."

I told her clearly that none of this is her fault, and that mocking someone's accent or face is bullying. I thanked her for keeping calm and bringing the evidence.

I took the screenshots to the principal during first period. The boys' parents have been called for tomorrow, and the posts were removed by noon. I have spoken to the class about respect and will check the class chat weekly. I asked Lalremsiami to come to me at once if anything else appears.

qa.q: Who started the memes about Lalremsiami?
qa.a: Pradeep started them; others joined in.

qa.q: What was Lalremsiami feeling when she came to the class teacher?
qa.a: Lalremsiami felt hurt and anxious, speaking very quietly, though her steady hands showed she was determined.

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami do that was wise?
qa.a: Lalremsiami did not reply, saved screenshots, blocked and reported the posts, and brought the evidence to a teacher.

qa.q: What is it like for Lalremsiami to have her accent mocked in front of the class?
qa.a: It is likely deeply hurtful and embarrassing, making her feel singled out for something she cannot and should not have to change.

grounding: It shows a teen mocked by classmates with memes and edited photos, who does not retaliate, saves screenshots, reports and tells a trusted adult, and is told it is not her fault.
